title: Zack Snyder (‘Batman v Superman’) takes a beating for his new movie: “An utter disgrace from start to finish” - Diario AS
content: Zack Snyder’s new film premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival amid scathing reviews, though some viewers praise its action scenes. Zack Snyder just can’t catch a break. After Netflix canceled his ambitious ‘Rebel Moon’ universe following scathing reviews of his only two films, the director of ’300′ and ‘Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice,’ has tried to return to the spotlight without any success. His latest film, ‘The Last Photograph,’ premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival, and critics have not hesitated to label it the worst of his career. Snyder is the screenwriter, producer, and director of ‘The Last Photograph’, which follows a former DEA agent who travels to the mountains of South America to find his missing nephews after their parents—diplomats—were murdered. Starring relatively unknown actors such as Stuart Martin (‘The Medici’) and Fra Free (the 2012 film ‘Les Misérables’), the film was panned following its premiere at the Canadian film festival. “One of the worst to ever play this festival. APOCALYPSE NO. Just unabashedly shit on every level, an excercise in incompetence and hubris, and an embarrassment to have been screened,” said Jason Gorber. “By the end, I genuinely wanted this to be the last film I ever have to see from him. Snyder desperately needs to stop shooting his own movies and return to adapting material strong enough to better withstand his worst overindulgences,” commented Matt Neglia. Canadian TikToker DawsOnScreen, who specializes in film, is no less explicit: “An utter disgrace from start to finish. It is Snyder at his most unfiltered, with no studio intervention and is the films largest problem.” Not everyone was left disappointed by ‘The Last Photograph,’ as there’s even a comment asking Snyder to adapt one of the most celebrated video game franchises of the 21st century. “The action was brutal. But that opening scene… wow! That guy should direct the live-action Call of Duty movie.” Unfortunately (or perhaps not), it’s too late, because the Call of Duty movie already has a director—none other than Peter Berg (‘Hancock,’ ‘The Darkest Hour’). Just a few weeks ago, Snyder fans had some hope that the DC Snyderverse would be restored, as the director was photographed at Warner Bros. Studios in a photo posted on his Instagram profile. However, it was confirmed that he was only there to watch a movie—specifically, a commemorative screening of ‘Excalibur’. Despite the situation surrounding James Gunn’s DC Universe—where his role remains uncertain—there is no indication that we will ever see Snyder directing another film featuring Batman, Superman, or any of the characters from the Distinguished Competition. title: Calvert-Lewin stars but Botman struggles - player ratings for Leeds v Newcastle - bbc.co.uk
content: Dominic Calvert-Lewin wreaked havoc as Leeds United moved up to third place in the Premier League table following a 4-1 win against Newcastle United at Elland Road. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. James Trafford: A relatively comfortable night against his former suitors. A couple of nervy clearances early on but went on to make an important save to deny Harvey Barnes. 7 James Justin: Teasing cross set up Leeds' second goal. Has become a key component in this system. 7 Nico Elvedi: Only his second Premier League start yet already looks at home at Elland Road. Solid at the back but got it all wrong at the other end after volleying wide at the back post when unmarked. 7 Tarik Muharemovic: The club's player of the month for August for a reason. Made it look rather comfortable at the back on Monday night. 7 Jayden Bogle: Second goal credited to him. Did not know much about it, but has found his shooting boots after his goal at Brighton last time out in the league. Twice forced Lukas Hornicek into big saves before second goal took final touch off him. A real threat. 8 Anton Stach: Won a corner inside 32 seconds. That set the tone for Leeds' relentless display, even if he later wasted chance to score. 7 Ethan Ampadu: Ensured Leeds kept pushing for more as he barked instructions. Saw Dominic Calvert-Lewin inadvertently block a vicious goalbound effort. 7 Ao Tanaka: His goal took two heavy deflections but had the confidence to take the shot. Looking back to his best in recent weeks even if he was relieved to see one misplaced pass unpunished. 7 Gabriel Gudmundsson: Caused Newcastle real problems with his runs down the left. Looked more a winger than a wing-back. 7 Noah Okafor: Fine strike for Leeds' fourth, having also coolly pulled the ball back for Tanaka to let fly for his side's opener. 8 Dominic Calvert-Lewin: Just loves this fixture. A trademark header came off Bogle for Leeds' second and then showed other side of his game to finish calmly on the floor for the hosts' third. Has scored eight goals against Newcastle - more than any other side. 9 Melvin Bard (on 72, Gudmundsson): Perfect environment to make his Premier League debut. 6 Brenden Aaronson (on 72, Tanaka): Lots of energy. 6 Lukas Hornicek: This would have been even uglier for the visitors were it not for Hornicek making fine saves to twice deny Bogle and also to foil Calvert-Lewin. 6 Amar Dedic: Shook off hamstring issue to start, but a tough night as Leeds repeatedly targeted his flank. 4 Malick Thiaw: Captain for night but this was far from a captain's performance. Beaten easily by Calvert-Lewin for Leeds' second goal, slapped turf in frustration after the striker fired past him for the third and then failed to block Okafor's fourth. 3 Sven Botman: Like Thiaw, could not cope with Calvert-Lewin and was skinned so easily for Leeds' second goal. 3 Lewis Hall: Dragged out of position in build-up of Leeds' second goal. Not the night he had in mind after signing a new deal. 4 Nico Gonzalez: Belatedly came off after just 19 minutes after the ball struck him in the head in the early stages. 5 Lewis Miley: Little he could do for deflection for Tanaka's goal, but was overrawed by Leeds' tenacious midfield. Had little time to find passing rhythm. 4 Jacob Murphy: Continued in injured Anthony Elanga's absence, but did not offer enough protection and caused Leeds few problems going the other way. 3 Yoane Wissa: Created Newcastle's best chance and at least battled and chased, even if his final ball was not always great. 5 Harvey Barnes: Has a fearsome record against Leeds and eyes lit up when he danced inside the box only for Trafford to deny him. 5 Matias Fernandez-Pardo: Full debut following his £51.4m move from Lille. Had little to feed off as Newcastle repeatedly played long balls forward. 4 Sean Steur (on 19, Gonzalez): Thrown into the cauldron after Gonzalez went off. Could do little about deflection before Leeds' first goal but gave the ball away in build up to Leeds' second. Eighteen-year-old will learn from experience. 4 Bazoumana Toure (on 58, Murphy) So rapid and pulled one back. Bright cameo as he pushes for a start. 6 Joe Willock (on 58, Fernandez-Pardo): One decent chance landed on roof of net from tight angle. 5 Tino Livramento (on 58, Dedic): Another step on return from injury. Set up Toure's consolation. 6 Aladji Bamba (on 79, Miley): A rare sighting following his summer move from Monaco. 5 After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. Entirely handcrafted in Italy, it’s built with 100 percent black patent leather, with the deep shine that elongates the leg. The adjustable ankle strap ensures a secure, tailored fit, while the leather sole with pearl detail is the discreet signature that sets every Aleví Milano pair apart. They retail for $885. If you've ever wanted to take a baseball bat to a Flock camera, you can now do it without getting arrested. The only catch is that you'll have to do it inside Grand Theft Auto V. Artist Morry Kolman created a new mod called Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader, or GTALPR. It puts 235 Flock-style cameras around Los Santos and actually pays players to destroy them. While playing, you can smash or shoot one and pick up what's left for $600 in game money. The cameras also photograph cars passing by, which can make dealing with the police a lot more annoying. Kolman notes on the project's website that destroying real Flock cameras is illegal and, they won't drop $600 if you do it. Embedded media follows. Please allow a moment for it to load. According to the official project page, 235 wasn't random. When Kolman made the mod, it was about one-tenth of the number of Flock cameras being tracked in Los Angeles County. That makes sense for GTA V, since Los Santos is heavily based on Los Angeles. Kolman even found a few places where the real and fictional maps line up closely enough to put cameras in roughly the same spots. Players get $600 for each destroyed camera because that is the estimated value of the parts inside a Flock camera. Kolman got the number from a hardware teardown of a Flock Falcon Flex by the group Eyes Off Cedar Rapids. You can also turn destroying them into a competition with yourself. The mod keeps track of your fastest time for taking out 10 cameras, 50 cameras or all 235. Of course, it wouldn't be much of a Flock camera mod if the cameras didn't occasionally cause problems. If you're already running from the cops and drive past one, it extends how long it takes to lose them. Kolman says some parts of the map have so many cameras that escaping police can become nearly impossible. Even driving around minding your own business isn't necessarily safe. Each time your vehicle enters a camera's field of view, there is a one-in-20, or 5%, chance that it will trigger a police chase for no reason. Kolman told WIRED that feature was inspired by real reports of innocent people being stopped because of errors involving automatic license plate readers. The virtual cameras will also photograph you as you pass. You can save those pictures later, complete with overlays made to look similar to the ones used on real Flock images. GTALPR is a single-player mod made for the PC version of GTA V Legacy. It should not be used with GTA Online, and it does not support GTA V Enhanced. You can download it through the GTALPR GitHub page, but it requires several installation steps and additional modding programs before you can start hunting down cameras. title: A contrite Fran Brown eyes quick turnaround v. ACC rival Pittsburgh on Thursday night - Sports Illustrated
content: The answers to the inquiring media's questions Monday were shorter and more predictable as Brown finished licking his wounds over the 21-18. tough-to-swallow opening conference game defeat to Cal last weekend in the Dome. It was a game that was certainly up for grabs heading late into the fourth quarter, and Brown quickly wanted to pivot ahead to the formidable Panthers challenge that awaits his squad Thursday night for the season's first road game at Acrisure Stadium (7:30 p.m. ET / ESPN). For some reason over the last 20 years under Greg Robinson, Doug Marrone, Scott Shafer, Dino Babers, and Brown, Syracuse stopped beating Pittsburgh. The 'Cuse has just two wins over Pitt (2023 and 2017) going back to 2013, coming, ironically, after SU amazingly lost only one game against the Panthers between 1984-2002 under Dick MacPherson and Paul Pasqualoni. Brown has so far not found success against his two peer northeastern ACC rival coaches Pat Narduzzi of Pitt, and BC's Bill O'Brien, going a combined 0-4 in his first two seasons. Without making his feelings too clear publicly, the winless record bothers Brown as a competitive coach. Now with just three days to prepare and build his team back up, Brown is focused on one of the advantages of a short week, especially when the last outcome did not turn out the way anyone wanted. "We just lost, (now) we have a chance to go play faster (schedule), that's what I like about it," Brown said Monday of the only weeknight game on this year's slate. "We get an opportunity to compete, go have fun, and have a chance to be 1-0 (this week)." But beating Pitt, which comes into this week's matchup at 2-0 off wins against Miami of Ohio and Central Florida, has been especially out of hand on the road, with an average margin of defeat at just over 12 points over the last five meetings in the Steel City. "It's going to be a tough game (my message to the team), you better be ready to go play," Brown said succinctly when asked about the challenges Pitt has caused the Orange football program over the last decade. "Coach Narduzzi is a good football coach, I like how he has his defense sound, they like to hit," Brown added. "On the offensive side of the ball, they create big plays. This conference is qurterback happy, right? Pitt's quarterback Mason Heintschel (18th this week nationally in passing efficiency/zero interceptions) is one of the better quarterbacks in the country." An apologetic Brown (to the team's supporters) has moved on from the Cal defeat, knowing the frustration level with an uneven performance has put Orange Nation into a cautious mode on predicting where things go next in the first road test. From quarterback Steve Angeli (will start at Pitt) throwing three picks, far too many penalties (the Orange have the most  penalties (27) and penalty yardage (257) of all 138 FBS teams), and shoddy special teams play that has cost the team points, Brown and the staff have their work cut out for them with short preparation time. None-the-less, head coaches tend to speak optimistically and are always looking to key in on the right motivational tools. "Do we find out how tough we are, do we go out and compete (Thursday)?," Brown asked rhetorically about his players. "We're going to keep working, we're moving on to the next football game, and hoping you (the supporters) can do the same thing to push and follow, and have our backs, and move on.                             | Last Update: September 14, 2026 In October 2022, Augusto V. visited an ear, nose and throat doctor and mentioned a strange feeling in his neck almost as an afterthought. His doctor ordered a CT scan that same day, which led to a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue. Because squamous cell carcinoma can spread, doctors ordered a PET scan of his body. The scan found a mass in Augusto’s left lung, separate from the tongue cancer. Doctors biopsied both areas, and before the lab results came back, a surgeon suspected mesothelioma based on the imaging. The biopsy confirmed pleural mesothelioma. His doctors staged it as stage 3 mesothelioma. His medical team recommended he see a mesothelioma specialist, and Augusto considered hospitals in Boston, New York and Houston. He chose Houston partly because he wanted his wife, Jackie, to feel comfortable there. “My wife was going to get lost and besides, it was almost wintertime,” Augusto tells us. “No way I’m putting her through that.” Family connections helped Augusto get an appointment with Dr. R. Taylor Ripley, a thoracic surgeon and mesothelioma specialist who practiced at Baylor College of Medicine at the time. Augusto says, “He gave me a real sense that he knew what he was doing,. He told me, ‘I know I can help you.’” At 69, Augusto first underwent surgery for tongue cancer in December 2022. He left the hospital weak and nearly 10 pounds lighter, so Dr. Ripley delayed his mesothelioma surgery for several weeks to give him time to regain his strength. In January 2023, Dr. Ripley performed an extrapleural pneumonectomy, removing the pleura, part of Augusto’s left lung, the pericardium and half of his diaphragm. The surgery lasted about 8 hours. Augusto spent 2 weeks in intensive care afterward and then several more days in a regular hospital room. He and his wife stayed in Houston for about 2 months so his care team could monitor his recovery closely before they returned to Florida. Dr. Ripley’s care continued after Augusto returned home. He gave Augusto his personal phone number and has answered his calls ever since, including once when Augusto reached out from out of town. “He gave me his personal number,” Augusto recalls. “He said, ‘Mr. V., you are my patient. Anytime you need to talk to me, you call me.’” “I take my hat off to him,” he says. “I mean, he saved my life.” Augusto returned home to Florida and started 4 rounds of chemotherapy in March 2023, with treatments every 3 weeks. A PET scan in June showed no evidence of disease. He spent the following months in Peru with his wife. After returning to Houston, a follow-up scan found the mesothelioma had returned. He started immunotherapy with Yervoy (ipilimumab) and Opdivo (nivolumab), receiving treatments every other week. Augusto developed a rash, persistent itching and fatigue. He later experienced fevers that lasted several weeks, requiring a hospital stay. “Everything else went out the window because it was fevers, fevers, fevers,” he says. Doctors spaced his treatments out to help manage side effects. “The day of the immunotherapy, I’m okay,” Augusto shares. “The third, fourth, fifth and sixth day, I go down.” His appetite disappears on those days. “I would say, ‘No, I don’t want any chicken soup. I would love a steak,’’” he tells us. “So my wife would run to make a steak and then I say, ‘No, I don’t want any.’” Augusto credits his wife, Jackie, with getting him through every part of his treatment and recovery. His surgery limits him from lifting more than 5 or 10 pounds, so she’s taken over nearly everything at home. “She drives for me. She cooks for me. She washes for me. She cleans for me,” he shares. “Nobody else but her is the person who has helped me with mesothelioma.” Jackie also stayed with Augusto through the long periods of treatment and recovery that followed his surgeries. Her support has remained an important part of how he manages his life while continuing treatment. Before his diagnosis, Augusto walked more than 6 miles a day along the shoreline near his home in Peru and enjoyed scuba diving in his free time. Treatment has slowed him down considerably and he admits some days it’s hard to find motivation to move much at all. “I just don’t feel like it,” he says. “That’s what the problem is.” Augusto is retired and currently splits his time between Florida and Peru while continuing treatment. He hopes to return to Peru permanently once his health allows, along with his old walking routine and scuba diving gear. He looks forward to celebrating his 73rd birthday in October and returning to the activities he enjoyed before his diagnosis. “I have all the equipment. I have a compressor and everything else in Peru, and I live right by the beach. I need to use it, and I’m going to use it,” Augusto says. Looking further into the future, Augusto and Jackie plan to help other cancer patients once his treatment allows for more travel. Rather than start a formal foundation, Augusto wants to work directly with people in need. “The people that I see desperate, I’m going to come to them and say, what is your problem? And I say, well, it happens that I just found the money. Here go and take it,” Augusto says. When asked what advice he’d give other survivors, Augusto points to the people around him, saying, “Strength and courage. Sometimes you don’t want to get out of bed. You have to listen to your wife, to your son, to your daughter.” He adds that the people who push you hardest usually want nothing in return. “All they want is for you to get better.” Stay up-to-date on treatment, research, clinical trials, doctors and survivors The information on this website is proprietary and protected. title: Liverpool v Tottenham Carabao Cup Predicted Line-Ups, Team News, and Match Preview - Yahoo Sports
content: Liverpool face Tottenham at Anfield for the Reds' third home game in a row. This one is in the Carabao Cup, with a place in the fourth round on the line. Following a draw against Fulham, Liverpool will be looking for a return to winning ways. Meanwhile, Tottenham have had a poor start to the season (currently sitting 17th place in the Premier League table), and will be thinking a win at Anfield would be the perfect springboard to kick-start their season. In his press conference earlier today, Andoni Iraola revealed: "We will see [against Tottenham] players we haven't seen [so far this season]". He also confirmed that Giorgi Mamardashvili "is going to start tomorrow" and that Joe Gomez "is available", but that "it's a matter of deciding how much he can play." Based on this information, here is the LFC Transfer Room's predicted Liverpool XI for tomorrow night's Carabao Cup clash: Giorgi Mamardashvili | Iraola confirmed that the Georgian keeper will start in goal for the first time this season. Luke Chambers | Given Iraola's hint toward starting some fresh faces tomorrow night, Chambers could be given the nod after Kostas Tsimikas's poor performance against Fulham. He could fulfil the 'Ronald Araujo role' from left-back in a rotated side. Virgil van Dijk | With limited options at centre-half, it would not be surprising to see the captain keep his place in the team. Wataru Endo | Endo could be in line for his first appearance of the season, playing in central defence alongside Virgil van Dijk to give Ronald Araujo and Jeremy Jacquet a rest. Jeremie Frimpong | Frimpong has not featured much for Liverpool in the last couple of weeks, so a Carabao Cup match represents a convenient point to bring him back into the fold with some minutes. Ryan Gravenberch | Gravenberch could be due for a back-to-back start if Iraola seeks to rest Alexis Mac Allister. Trey Nyoni | It would be very surprising to not see Nyoni play this one. Iraola will surely want to see how the youngster fares starting against Premier League opposition to decide whether he can be relied on more going forward. Dominik Szoboszlai | It would be interesting to see Szoboszlai return to the No. 10 position but in Iraola's new-look system. Rio Ngumoha | Rio had a lively cameo against Fulham and a good game against Atletico Madrid beforehand; he could be given the opportunity to build on his form against Tottenham. Cody Gakpo | A start for Gakpo is not out of the question, with the Dutchman in need of minutes to get back up to speed. Lewis Koumas | Alexander Isak has started every game for Liverpool this season and could definitely do with a rest. Koumas is a big favourite of Iraola, so it would make sense for him to be given a chance in this one. In his own press conference earlier today, Roberto de Zerbi revealed that Sandro Tonali will miss the game after receiving a knock in their last match, whilst Pedro Porro and Mykhailo Mudryk remain unavailable. Meanwhile, Destiny Udogie is fit to start, and Richarlison remains frozen out of Spurs' squad. Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, and Dejan Kulesevski are all still recovering from long-term injuries and are unavailable. title: Studs and duds from Colts' Week 1 loss v. Ravens - Yahoo Sports
content: The Baltimore Ravens cruised past the Indianapolis Colts in the team's 2026 regular-season opener. Let's take a look back at Sunday's performance with Indianapolis' studs and duds. It wasn't perfect -- Taylor did have a fumble, but he was one of the few bright spots for the Colts in this game. Taylor finished the game with 98 rushing yards on just 19 attempts with two rushing touchdowns. Baltimore was able to contain him early, but that often only lasts for so long. The Colts' defense had zero answers for Baltimore for much of the game. Both on the ground and through the air, the Ravens were able to generate explosive plays, averaging over 8.0 yards per play -- a massive amount. For some context, last season, the LA Rams' offense led the NFL in this category, averaging 6.1 yards per play. Lamar Jackson was efficient and also averaged a whopping 13.0 yards per play. Derrick Henry averaged nearly 6.0 yards per rush while running for 135 yards. The Ravens finished the game with 506 total yards on offense. As mentioned, Taylor had a good day on the ground, which included averaging 5.2 yards per attempt. The offensive line unit also surrendered just six total pressures over 140 combined pass-blocking snaps. This unit was supposed to be a strength of this Colts' team. But on Sunday, Lamar Jackson and the Ravens' pass game picked that unit apart. Jackson threw for 324 yards on just 17 completions. Zay Flowers totaled 150 receiving yards on five receptions. If the Colts' secondary doesn't play at a high level, it's going to be tough sledding for this defense that has pass rush questions. title: Colts early round draft pick plays zero snaps v. Ravens - Yahoo Sports
content: Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said last week that the Indianapolis Colts would rotate at the linebacker position. Well, in Week 1, that was mostly true, but surprisingly, it didn't include rookie second-round pick CJ Allen. As was expected, Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies were the starters on Sunday. Davis-Gaither would play 64 of the 68 defensive snaps, while Carlies played 42 snaps. Rotated in with Carlies was rookie Bryce Boettcher, who played 23 defensive snaps, according to PFF. Allen, however, did not see the field at all. He was the 53rd overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. Anarumo will speak with local reporters on Tuesday, at which point we should learn more about this development. What we do know is that Allen missed his share of time during training camp, particularly early on, navigating injuries. Missed practice time, especially for a rookie, are valuable reps that can't be replaced. We will see if this trend continues into Week 2. Carlies had a quiet game, which could potentially mean more opportunities for Boettcher, or perhaps we'll see Allen for the first time in the regular season against Kansas City. title: Robert V. “Bob” Withrow (1939-2026) - dailybulldog.com
content:
WELD — Robert V. “Bob” Withrow, a man defined by his unwavering integrity, love of hard work, and a lifelong passion for the natural world, passed away on Friday September 11th, 2026. He leaves behind a legacy of adventure and dedication. Born on April 17, 1939, in Mahnomen, Minnesota, Bob’s journey was shaped by the forests he loved and the family he cherished. Bob’s lifelong devotion to forestry began during his college years at St. John’s University and the University of Minnesota. His youth was filled with a vibrant spirit and the kind of grit rare today; he enthusiastically participated in high school athletics, music, and the Boy Scouts, while falling in love with fishing and hunting alongside his brother and father. He spent his college summers working as a forest firefighter in northern Idaho, hitchhiking back and forth between Minnesota and Idaho and collecting a lifetime of stories along the way. His studies also took him abroad to Germany, where he participated in a forestry exchange program in Bodman. An ROTC student, Bob underwent German language training in Monterey, California, before serving in the U.S. Army as an intelligence officer stationed in Bremerhaven, Germany. It was there that he met the love of his life, Ursula. Together, they began building their family and a life that would span 61 beautiful years of marriage. After his military service, Bob returned to Minnesota to earn a Master’s degree in Forestry Economics, launching a career with the Boise Cascade paper company. His work took his growing family from International Falls, Minnesota, to Boise, Idaho, and ultimately to the place that would capture his heart forever: Maine. Bob truly found his heaven on earth in the western mountains of Maine, especially in Weld, where he and Ursula built their dream house. He poured his energy into the land. His happiest hours were spent sailing the Maine coast, hunting in Bowmantown, and tending to the earth in the Rumford community garden and at the Hodges Schoolhouse in Phillips. A craftsman and a creator, he deeply enjoyed woodworking projects, including building alongside his brother, Tom, and friends at the Sky Theater in East Dixfield. A true highlight of his life was “Grandpa’s maple syrup” operation—a labor of love created alongside a close-knit group of friends, where hours were happily spent working in the woods and drinking coffee in the sugar shack. Bob’s deep connection to his community extended well beyond his hobbies. Believing in active citizenship, he dedicated his time to many volunteer roles throughout his life. He served on the local school board and library board, and shared his love for winter sports by volunteering with the Chisholm Ski Club at Black Mountain and the handicap ski program at Sunday River. Bob was always willing to lend his time, mind, and hard work to better the places he called home. Above all his pursuits, the true core of Bob’s life was simply being surrounded by his family and his wonderful network of friends. He maintained a relentless love of learning, a hunger for new experiences, and a steady, quiet sense of right and wrong. Bob leaves behind his beloved wife of 61 years, Ursula Fischer Withrow; his children, Karen (Anthony) Capone, Lisa Withrow Atkins, and Jeff (Marisa) Withrow; and his cherished grandchildren, Matt, Sam, Johanna, Allison, Amelia, Walter, and Maggie. He is also survived by his brother, Tom Withrow, and sister, Jean Withrow (Jim Haggerty). Bob was reunited in peace with his parents, Verne and Isabel Thoma Withrow, his deceased sister-in-law, Susan, and his deeply missed sons, Dan and Tim. Bob once said his best place to take a nap was on the mossy ground under the base of a tree in the woods. He is resting there now. Please join us to celebrate Bob’s role in our lives on Saturday, September 19, 2026, at the Weld Town Hall (23 School St, Weld, ME) from 2:00 PM to 4:30 PM. In lieu of flowers, donations may be made to the Weld Congregational Church, P.O. Box 98, Weld, ME 04285. Family and friends are encouraged to visit Bob’s Book of Memories at www.wilesrc.com to leave words of comfort, share memories, and photos. Honored to be providing cremation care to the family of Robert V. Withrow is Wiles Remembrance Center- Farmington. title: The Supercharged American Sedan Giving German Rivals Nightmares For The Last 5 Years - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update When asked about the best performance sedan that has ever existed, people may recall the mighty BMW M5 or even the Mercedes-Benz E63 with its thunderous noise. While it's not news that the Germans have been excellent at making performance sedans throughout the years, there is an American sedan that sticks to the original formula of a V8 engine paired with a manual transmission while its rivals switch to a smaller powertrains. The Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing is not only the last manual V8 sports sedan but also the ultimate choice for enthusiasts in 2026. Here is everything you need to know about this pure American sports sedan since it was introduced to the market back in 2022. This article looks at the Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing by model years, discussing all Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing generations including facelifts on sale in the USA. The standard CT5 received a facelift for the 2025 model and so does the CT5-V Blackwing. The facelift brings several exterior changes to the Blackwing, which include a wider grille along with daytime running lights that extend to the lower grille. There are also new air vents below the headlights to help people better distinguish the Blackwing from a regular CT5. Lastly, as least as far as aesthetics are involved, three new metallic paints are available for the 2025 model year onwards, along with a new LED animation to greet the driver when approaching the vehicle. The powertrain remains unchanged after the facelift. The same 6.2-liter supercharged V8 produces 668 horsepower and 656 pound-feet of torque. Power is sent to the rear wheels only via a six-speed manual or an optional 10-speed automatic transmission. Other performance-oriented features such as launch control, limited-slip differential and traction management can all be found on the CT5-V Blackwing. The facelift also brings several changes to the interior of the Blackwing. The central screen is now replaced with a 33-inch display screen that boasts 9K resolution. Half of the display runs a Google-based operating system with Google Maps and Google Assistant built in. At the same time, the old wireless connectivity, onboard Wi-Fi and 16-speaker AKG sound system still come as standard. Cadillac has announced that 2026 will be the last year for the supercharged V8 and manual transmission formula. While the new CT5 will still get an internal combustion powertrain, the days of a roaring V8 paired with a manual transmission might soon be over. To celebrate its first Formula One Grand Prix in the USA, Cadillac introduced the 2026 CT5-V Blackwing F1 Collector Series for the 2026 model year. To make this special edition Blackwing go even faster, a new supercharger was put into the Blackwing F1 Collector Series which produces 685 horsepower and 673 pound-feet of torque. Combined with the fact that only 26 of these special-edition Blackwings will be produced, this is not only the fastest CT5 but also the rarest of its kind. Other than the increase in horsepower output, Cadillac has also styled the F1 Collector Series in a unique way to make it stand out when compared to a regular CT5-V Blackwing. To start with, a special color scheme named the Midnight Stone Front was applied to the entire body along with several motorsport-themed designs throughout the entire vehicle. Such as the red F1 logo on the rear wing, the FIA logo on the side skirts as well as the F1 emblem that show up on the headrests and a 3D-printed shift knob. Every detail is there to remind you of its motorsport pedigree. With a list price of $260,000, the F1 Collector Series has certainly got a hefty price tag. However, considering only 26 will ever be built, along with the fact that CT5-V Blackwings are known to hold their value better than other performance sedans on the market, the F1 Collector Series could be a worthy investment if you are looking for something truly special. Being the rightful successor of the outgoing CTS-V, the CT5-V Blackwing was more than just a regular CT5 with some extra ponies and an aggressive appearance. This Cadillac performance sedan was truly the last of its kind. While other manufacturers were switching to a more efficient hybrid powertrain and a smaller displacement engine, Cadillac still maintained the old-school formula by pairing a 6.2-liter supercharged V8 engine that produces 668 hp and 656 lb-ft of torque with a rear-wheel-drive chassis. The fun didn't stop there. Apart from a vicious supercharged V8 engine up in the front, Cadillac didn't forget that the key element that makes a vehicle fun lies in the engagement between the car and the driver. The CT5-V Blackwing was the last sports sedan on the market to come standard with a manual transmission. While there was also a 10-speed automatic as an option, we all know which was the better option if you were looking for ultimate driving pleasure. With the standard six-speed manual, the CT5-V Blackwing could hit 60 mph in 3.6 seconds, while the 10-speed automatic was capable of the same in 3.5 seconds. The interior layout of the CT5-V Blackwing was largely the same when compared with the standard CT5. The main difference lay within the features and details. To start with, the Blackwing came with leather upholstery and front seats that were both heated and ventilated. As for technology and infotainment, you got a 10-inch touchscreen display with wireless CarPlay and Android Auto along with a 4G hotspot feature. To further emphasize the premium feel of the Blackwing, the standard Bose stereo system was replaced by a 16-speaker AKG sound system. In the modern automotive landscape, it's easy to make a car run fast in a straight line. With the introduction of the new electric performance sedan, the numbers game has got to a point where it is almost out of control. You have a family sedan that pushes over 1,000 horsepower and reaches 60 mph in less than two seconds. But Cadillac understands being the first in the straight line doesn't necessarily make a vehicle fun and desirable. That's where the Blackwing nameplate truly shines when compared to other rivals on the market. If you are not familiar with the name Blackwing, you can view it as the brand's ultimate performance version, even higher than the already established V models that people might be familiar with. To make the CT5-V Blackwing stand out against other performance sedans on the market, Cadillac embedded a few tricks within the CT5-V Blackwing. The first thing is the six-speed manual transmission sourced from transmission specialists Tremec. This manual transmission features a No-Lift Shift function and Active Rev-Matching to make every acceleration a blast in the CT5-V Blackwing. Underneath the chassis, the Blackwing features an electronically managed rear differential, MagneRide Adaptive damper system along with optional carbon ceramic brakes to make sure you have enough confidence while behind the wheel of a Blackwing. "Hopping into the Cadillac feels like a time capsule, a reminder of a time when weight and complexity were the enemies of performance. The CT5-V Blackwing feels like the ultimate mid-2000s luxury sedan, built in 2024 with modern technology and power." - Jared Rosenholtz, Former Editor-at-Large, CarBuzz We want to hear from you. title: Reading v Brentford - match preview, kick-off time and more - Brentford FC
content: Analysis, team news, match officials and more - here's everything you need to know ahead of the game. Brentford make the short trip to Select Car Leasing Stadium to take on Reading in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night - no doubt aware that their League One opponents pack a punch on their own patch. Leam Richardson's Royals currently sit 14th in the third tier after a 2-1 reverse away at Cambridge last weekend, but have hit three or more goals in exactly half of their games across all competitions this term. Spearheaded by League One's current top scorer Jack Marriott, the Berkshire outfit average 17.4 shots per 90 this season and have scored more goals at home (11) than any other team in the division. Across the EFL, only Championship sides Southampton (15) and West Ham United (14) have been more prolific on home turf. With five of their 12 league goals (42 per cent) scored on the counter attack, the Royals seem well-equipped to cause problems on the break - with Marriott snaffling two strikes from such situations already. The Bees will also need to keep an eye on former Brentford B winger Kyreece Lisbie, who ranks among League One's most creative players with three assists and 11 key passes to his name this season. Still unbeaten during the current campaign, Brentford travel to Berkshire knowing their hosts will be desperate to cause a cup upset, and Keith Andrews will want his side to switch on early - particularly given Reading's penchant for starting well. Across their six league games this season, the Royals have scored more first-half goals (eight) than any other side in League One - six of those arriving in the 15 minutes leading up to half-time. What's more, Reading have conceded just one goal themselves prior to the interval. The Bees hit Championship side Birmingham City for six in a 6-1 win at St Andrew's in the second round, with summer signing Callum Wilson netting his first goal for the club, and they will hope their mobility and physicality in forward areas can trouble their hosts on Tuesday. Reading's defensive numbers, however, suggest they will make the Bees work for their opportunities. The Royals have conceded fewer shots per game (nine) than any team in League One this season and Richardson will hope his backline can blunt Brentford's attacking threat. In the summer of 2025, former Wycombe Wanderers owner Rob Couhig and Todd Trosclair completed their takeover of Reading. Purchasing the club from disqualified former owner Dai Yongge had been a complex process, and it took two attempts to finally get it over the line. The Royals had been in a precarious position before that and, while they were not out of the woods financially, their immediate future was secure. In spite of the way things were starting to progress off the pitch, to begin with, that was not the case on it. Noel Hunt's side did not win any of their first five League One games in 2025/26 and, when they had only won three of their first 14, Couhig announced the decision to terminate his contract. "My duty is to make the decisions I believe give this club the best chance of long-term success," he said in a statement on the club's official website. "This is one of those decisions - not an easy one, but a necessary one." On 28 October, two days after Hunt's exit, in came Leam Richardson. He signed an 18-month deal and arrived with pedigree, having steered Wigan Athletic to the League One title in 2021/22 with 92 points. Before long, Reading were on the right track and looking upwards after 11 wins in his first 22 league games in charge. A season that had begun with them looking over their shoulders had turned into something more and, with eight games to play, Richardson's side found themselves in the play-off places. The form across the final 11 games was nightmarish, however. Reading won only twice, collecting nine points from a possible 33, and their play-off hopes evaporated. They finished 12th in the end, 12 points behind Stevenage, who finished sixth. "When I first came in, it was always going to be a big project. It was not going to happen overnight," said Richardson afterwards. "We're going to address things internally and externally because this club needs it and demands it. We've got a big transfer window coming, we've got a big summer coming. "It's my job and I'm full of optimism for it, I know what this league takes and how to move forward. That's what we'll be concentrating on." A big window was promised, and that's what Reading had. They sold academy product Kelvin Ehibhationmhan to Danish side Horsens, before bringing in former Brentford B player Kyreece Lisbie, Udoka-Godwin-Malife and Jamie Reid, as well as highly rated England Under-21s international George Earthy from West Ham. Former Hannover defender Josh Knight joined on loan from Portsmouth, while Josh Stokes arrived on loan from Bristol City. Now, the season has not panned out exactly as Richardson would have hoped so far, but there have certainly been encouraging signs. They have won two penalty shoot-outs in cup competitions and thumped five past Mansfield Town in League One earlier this month. Last time out, they took the lead against early high-flyers Cambridge, but lost 2-1. "We won't hang around on the result for too long because we're in a good place at the minute and we'll certainly build from it," Richardson said. It is no secret Reading want more this season. In Hot off the Press, Ramy Abou-Setta said "they believe they are a Championship team". From the Football League's divisional rebrand in 2004/05 until their relegation in 2022/23, they had not spent a single season below the second tier. This season will be their fourth in succession in the third. Now it's down to Richardson and his men to turn promise into promotion and end that run. Leam Richardson started his career at Blackburn Rovers in the mid-1990s and made his one and only appearance for Rovers against Leeds United - his hometown club, where he used to have a season ticket as a child - in a 1-0 Worthington Cup defeat at Elland Road in October 1999. At the end of that season, he made the half-hour trip south to join Bolton Wanderers. He made 15 appearances in 2000/01, then made his Premier League debut - ironically, also against Leeds - in September 2001. The defender spent the best part of the next two seasons out on loan in Division Two, first at Notts County, then at Blackpool. In the summer of 2003, he joined the latter on a permanent basis and went on to play 63 times in all competitions, scoring once. Following his release, he joined Conference side Accrington Stanley and played a key role as they won the title and were promoted to the Football League for the first time since the club was re-established in 1968. Richardson went on to make 126 appearances for Stanley in all, with the last coming in December 2011. He stepped up to become caretaker after John Coleman's exit the following month and was appointed permanently in November 2012, a matter of weeks before his 33rd birthday. However, in April 2013, he moved on to Chesterfield to become Paul Cook's assistant and took up the same role under Cook at Portsmouth in 2015 and at Wigan in 2017. Richardson remained at Wigan after Cook's departure in the summer of 2020 and took caretaker charge during a turbulent period for the club. After Cook took over at Ipswich Town the following March, Richardson stayed with the Latics rather than reuniting with his former boss and, in April 2021, signed a three-year deal to become manager. His side won the Sky Bet League One title in 2021/22, but after a poor start to life back in the Championship, he was sacked in November 2022. A four-month stint at Rotherham United, between December 2023 and April 2024, came next and, just over 18 months later, he signed a contract running until the summer of 2027 at Reading. Ramy Abou-Setta, Reading reporter for the Reading Chronicle, explains what Brentford can expect from Leam Richardson's side. "Richardson plays a 4-2-3-1 as his staple formation," he told brentfordfc.com. "It can change in attacking phases to a 3-4-2-1 or a 3-4-3, depending on how he wants to shape his attack; whether he wants more wide players or whether he wants the no.10 to act as a second striker. "In possession, they will play with three at the back and out of possession, they will play with four at the back. He loves using the full-backs to help out in attack and be the extra man in the box or an extra passing option. "The ball is always set to go to Marriott, but now they have Jamie Reid and Jacob Brown as well and they are completely different profiles of striker, so the tactics change depending on who the no.9 is. "But in terms of the team around the striker, that does not tend to change. They are set in terms of how Richardson wants them to play; it is literally just a straight swap when it comes to who is playing up front." Kaye Furo will miss Brentford's Carabao Cup round three tie against Reading after undergoing an operation on Monday morning. Furo had been in line to start at Select Car Leasing Stadium, but picked up an injury in training in the build-up to the game. “I would’ve started him against Reading because I felt he deserved it and was in that type of space,” said Keith Andrews in his pre-match press conference. The Bees head coach also confirmed that centre-back Benjamin Fredrick is expected to be involved. “He hasn’t had a lot of football but has come back in the last couple of weeks,” Andrews added. “We decided not to play him in the B-team game on Sunday to make sure he was in the right place to be available for our game against Reading. Tom Nield will take charge of Brentford's Carabao Cup round three tie against Reading on Tuesday night. Nield refereed 27 games across all competitions last season, showing 100 yellow cards and one red. The official has overseen four fixtures so far this term, including Championship meetings between Swansea City and Sheffield United, Wolverhampton Wanderers and Stoke City, and Charlton Athletic and Queens Park Rangers. Brentford moved to the top of the Championship with a 3-1 victory over Reading at Madejski Stadium. Lucas João's penalty gave the Royals the lead midway through the first half, before Josh Dasilva levelled nine minutes before the interval. The contest remained level until the closing stages, when Dasilva struck his second of the night in the 86th minute and Ivan Toney added a third two minutes later. The victory extended Thomas Frank's side's unbeaten league run to 21 games and moved the Bees two points clear at the top of the Championship. title: Flamengo v Independiente del Valle, second leg of the CONMEBOL Libertadores quarter-finals: kick-off time, teams and how to watch the match - ssodigital.conmebol.com
content: Junior Sornoza is one match away from a round number. If he plays on Thursday at the Maracanã, Independiente del Valle's number 10 will reach 50 matches for the club in the CONMEBOL Libertadores, and he is already the player with the most appearances, goals and assists in the 'Matagigantes'' history in the competition, with 49, 20 and 11, respectively. He will do so two goals down against a defending champion that barely knows what it is to trail. In the entire edition, Leonardo Jardim's side have been behind for just 13 minutes and 54 seconds, 1.7% of the time played, the lowest percentage in the competition, and it happened only once, away to Cruzeiro in the Round of 16. In Quito they did what no visitor had done in the six previous meetings between the two: win. They did it with two shots on target, Bruno Henrique's, the man Jardim chose over Pedro for the altitude, and Léo Pereira's header, and ended a run of seven knockout matches without a win outside Brazil. The Maracanã, moreover, is their safe place. Flamengo have played 28 knockout matches in the competition at home and in 26 achieved a result that, if repeated against Independiente del Valle, would see them through; they won 12 of their last 13 knockout games at home, with the only defeat against Peñarol in 2024, 0-1. And whenever they won the first leg away, they advanced in six of seven occasions, including the five most recent. The exception is distant: 2008, 4-2 in Mexico against América and 0-3 in Brazil. Independiente del Valle, however, have reasons not to give up. Joaquín Papa's side dominated the first leg with 18 shots and a Carlos González effort off the post, and in Brazil they have four wins in CONMEBOL competitions: against Corinthians in the 2019 CONMEBOL Sudamericana semifinals, against Grêmio in the 2021 Third Stage, against América Mineiro in 2022 and against Corinthians again in 2023. Since 2019, only Racing and Defensa y Justicia have as many away wins against Brazilian sides in those competitions. Tie to be decided: Independiente del Valle need to win by two goals to force penalties and by three to qualify; Flamengo go through with any other result. Jardim summed it up in Quito in one sentence: "We took an important step, not a decisive one." On Thursday we will find out whether he was right. Stadium: Jornalista Mário Filho (Maracanã), Rio de Janeiro Date and time: Thursday, September 17, 9:30 PM (Argentina time)

title: Corinthians v Estudiantes, second leg of the CONMEBOL Libertadores quarter-finals: kick-off time, teams and how to watch the match - ssodigital.conmebol.com
content: Precedents split down the middle for 90 decisive minutes. Corinthians advanced in seven of the eight occasions on which they drew the first leg away in the CONMEBOL Libertadores, three of them in the 2012 title-winning campaign, and won all three quarterfinal second legs they have played at home, the last on the way to that crown: 1-0 against Vasco da Gama at the Pacaembu. Estudiantes, on the other side, are unbeaten in five of their last six away matches in knockout rounds of the competition, with four clean sheets, and the only second leg in that run was the 3-0 against Universidad Católica in this year's Round of 16. The 1-1 in La Plata had two halves with different owners. Alexis Castro opened the scoring in the 4th minute of the first half, the second-fastest goal in the 'Pincha's' history in a knockout round of the competition, from a Hugo Souza rebound. Kaio César equalized 4 minutes into the second half with an assist from Rodrigo Garro, the edition's assist leader with five, and that goal was Corinthians' first as visitors in the knockout stages since Romarinho's in the 2012 final against Boca. Souza finished with five saves, the last in stoppage time from a Joaquín Correa header. The styles, moreover, are opposites. Corinthians have the highest home possession average of the edition since the start of the group stage, at 67%; Estudiantes average 41% away from home and in La Plata generated half of their 14 shots from set pieces, including Castro's goal from a corner. Alexander Medina's side, four-time champions of America, will be without Gastón Benedetti, suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards, and lean on Guido Carrillo, the top scorer in their history in the competition with 14 goals. Fernando Diniz's team, the 2023 champion with Fluminense, look to repeat at the Neo Química Arena their habit of settling ties at home. Date and time: Wednesday, September 16, 9:30 PM (Argentina time)

title: The Sony a7 V Has Been Topped the Charts for 7 of the First 8 Months of 2026 - PetaPixel
content: The Sony a7 V Has Been Topped the Charts for 7 of the First 8 Months of 2026 August sales charts from Japan have arrived, telling a very similar story as nearly all of the other months this year: the Sony a7 V is selling extremely well. When the Sony a7 V debuted on Map Camera’s sales charts in December, it outsold the next four cameras combined. It then stayed atop the sales charts in January, February, March, and April. After briefly losing its top spot in May, the a7 V returned to the top of the sales charts in June, July, and now August. The Sony a7 V has been the best-selling new digital camera at Map Camera in seven of eight months in 2026 and eight of the last nine. It’s an extremely impressive run, and the a7 V’s performance at Map Camera speaks to the camera’s appeal among enthusiast-level photographers. Map Camera is one of Japan’s largest dedicated photography retailers and caters to relatively serious shooters. However, the a7 V still has broad appeal in Japan, many months after its release. For the August BCN Rankings, which capture a wider swath of retail locations, including department stores, the Sony a7 V is still in fifth spot on the sales charts. It’s behind significantly less expensive models like the Canon EOS R10 and EOS R50 APS-C cameras and the Sony ZV-E10 II vlogging camera. The a7 V is the priciest camera in BCN’s rankings by a significant margin. Meanwhile, over in the rest of Map Camera’s sales charts, there are a lot of other familiar faces. With improved production numbers, Ricoh’s very popular GR IV compact camera jumped up to second place, up from 10th in June and fifth in July. Another popular compact camera landed in third place: the Fujifilm X100VI. This camera launched in early 2024 and has been mired in supply issues. However, demand hasn’t wavered yet. Map Camera notes that with both the GR IV and X100VI, it easily sells all of the models it can get from Ricoh and Fujifilm. The rest of the top 10, starting in fourth place, includes the Canon PowerShot SX740 HS, the Sony a6700, the Fujifilm X-M5, the DJI Osmo Pocket 4P, the Fujifilm X-T30 III, the Canon PowerShot G7X Mark III, and the Canon EOS R6 Mark II. There’s little reason to think the a7 V won’t maintain its position in September, although it will be interesting to see a camera like the OM System PEN performs the following month. Early reports out of Japan suggest the camera is very popular with preorders. Image creditsSony a7 V product photo by Erin Thomson for PetaPixel. title: The “born free and equal” clauses and the noxious Buck v. Bell - SCOTUSblog
content: This is the fifth of seven introductory articles on the relevance for constitutional law and the Supreme Court of the “born free and equal” clauses, which appeared in the Declaration of Independence and in six out of 12 state constitutions when the federal Bill of Rights was ratified in 1791, in 24 out of 37 state constitutions when the 14th Amendment was ratified in 1868, and is in 37 out of 50 state constitutions today. The “born free and equal” clause of the Massachusetts Constitution of 1780, for example, provided that: In my initial articles, I showed that the “born free and equal” idea is deeply rooted in American history and tradition as that phrase is used in such correctly decided cases as Washington v. Glucksberg (rejecting a right to assisted suicide), McDonald v. City of Chicago (recognizing that the Second Amendment’s right to own a handgun for self-protection extends to the states), and Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization (overturning Roe v. Wade). In the second and third article, I argued that while the 14th Amendment does not give rise to a “right to privacy,” it does through the privileges or immunities clause constitutionalize the “born free and equal” clauses, subject to rational basis review, which justifies the outcome, although not the opinions in 1965’s Griswold v. Connecticut (holding that states may not criminalize the use of contraceptives by married couples) and in 2003’s Lawrence v. Texas (holding that states may not criminalize same-sex “sodomy”). And in my fourth article, I examined the application of the “born free and equal” clauses to yet another famous “right to privacy” case: 2015’s decision in Obergefell v. Hodges, which correctly found a national constitutional right to same-sex civil marriages. Today I turn to one of the most atrocious rulings in Supreme Court history: the 1927 case of Buck v. Bell, in which the court, 8-1, upheld a model eugenics statute. Specifically, a Virginia act allowed the compulsory sterilization, for the supposed “protection and health of the state,” of anyone who was deemed by a “social worker” to have genes resulting in feeblemindedness, unfitness, or an intellectual disability. Only a perfunctory hearing was allowed to those who were compulsorily sterilized. This statute did not come out of nowhere. Rather, such eugenics laws were first championed in 1883 by the social Darwinist Sir Francis Galton, a second cousin of Charles Darwin who chillingly believed that there were many different human “races” on the earth and that those races of human beings were competing for what psychologist and philosopher Herbert Spencer called “the survival of the fittest.” Galton, who was fascinated by the concept of animal breeding of dogs and racehorses, dreamed of applying this to human beings so as to promote the most intelligent, physically strong, and beautiful or handsome of them. (Darwin himself had hinted at such an idea in “The Origin of Species,” and mentioned it in his 1871 book “The Descent of Man.”) Support for eugenics laws became an orthodox staple of the creed of the Progressive Era. In one letter, President Theodore Roosevelt stated that: Woodrow Wilson, the other major Progressive politician of the first part of the 20th century, signed a eugenics bill into law as governor of New Jersey. Other famous eugenicists included William Howard Taft; Margaret Sanger (the founder of Planned Parenthood); and Winston Churchill. Indeed, as home secretary from 1910 to 1911, Churchill argued for eugenic government intervention regarding people categorized at the time as “feeble-minded” or “insane.” In addition, major early philanthropic foundations like the Carnegie Institution and the Rockefeller Foundation provided extensive financial grants to eugenics organizations, such as the Eugenics Record Office at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, under the direction of leaders and trustees who subscribed to the pseudoscience of the era. This extended to the universities as well. James Rowland Angell, who was president of Yale from 1921 t0 1937, and Charles William Eliot, who was president of Harvard from 1869 to 1909, were outspoken and virulent eugenics supporters. (Elliott served as a vice president to the first International Eugenics Congress held in London in 1912.) The court itself perhaps most prominently embraced this movement in Buck v. Bell. In upholding Virginia’s compulsory sterilization law, Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes, Jr. wrote for the majority that: In the wake of the Supreme Court’s ruling, 70,000 Americans were compulsorily sterilized, and 32 states ended up adopting compulsory sterilization statutes like Virginia’s. Nazi jurists and race hygienists studied U.S. sterilization statutes, such as California’s eugenics programs, as well as the Buck v. Bell decision. These laws inspired Adolf Hitler’s Nazi government to pass a German eugenics law in July 1933 entitled a “Law for the Prevention of Offspring with Hereditary Diseases” a few months after the Nazis came to power. Ultimately, 400,000 people were sterilized by the German law. The same racist ideology that led to these compulsory sterilizations in Hitler’s Nazi Germany undoubtedly helped fuel the ideas behind the Holocaust. Such ideas could not be in greater contrast to the Lockean principle that “All men are born free and equal.” That idea was thriving in the 1780’s when the Constitution was adopted; it was thriving during Reconstruction and in President Abraham Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address; but by 1912 it had effectively died out. The “born free and equal” idea only reemerged in 1948 as an Article I right in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights after the horrors of the Nazis and the Holocaust began coming to light. Buck v. Bell was egregiously wrong not only as a matter of morals, but under the “birthright equality” principle that underlies the citizenship clause of the 14th Amendment. Citizens, as I explained in my prior articles, are born equal (i.e., they are born to be neither slaves nor lords). The citizenship clause grants equal rights unto the feeble-minded and the geniuses of this world alike. The right to have children, like the right to marry (the purpose of which is often to have children) is obviously deeply rooted in American history and tradition. The Preamble of our Constitution states that one of the six purposes of that document is: “To secure the Blessings of Liberty to ourselves and our Posterity”. It goes without saying, I think, that a government which is compulsorily sterilizing its citizens based on a social worker’s finding of feeblemindedness is not securing the “Blessings of Liberty to ourselves and our Posterity.” The landmark 1823 decision of Corfield v. Coryell, which I have previously said is the 14th Amendment’s version of the “born free and equal” clauses, stated that: As noted, Americans cannot “enjoy … life and liberty” or “pursue and obtain happiness and safety” if they face the risk of compulsorily sterilization. But can such laws then be justified under Coryell’s rational basis test (in bold), i.e., that such laws are “just” and are enacted for the “general good of the whole [people]?” Certainly not. A government that could compulsorily sterilize the feeble-minded would also be able to compulsorily sterilize any population that has fallen out of favor, whether Jewish or Black people, Native Americans, or Latinos. Nor, even if such a policy for the “feebleminded” was justified, could it be properly implemented (as was true in Buck’s very own case). The Supreme Court distinguished but did not overrule Buck v. Bell in 1942’s Skinner v. Oklahoma after it became terribly apparent what eugenics led to. Someday, the Supreme Court should formally overrule this terrible precedent. In the meantime, Harvard Law School should cancel its annual, prestigious “Oliver Wendell Holmes Lecture.” Professor Steven Gow Calabresi is the Clayton J. & Henry R. title: Liverpool v Tottenham Hotspur: Team news - Liverpool FC
content:
Andoni Iraola will carefully assess his Liverpool squad to determine who is ready to start Tuesday night's Carabao Cup tie with Tottenham Hotspur. A busy period for the Reds continues with Premier League opposition arriving at Anfield in the third round of the League Cup. There will be at least one change from the side that began the draw against Fulham at the weekend, with Iraola confirming Giorgi Mamardashvili is set to be in goal. Discussing his selection plans, the Liverpool head coach told reporters on Monday: "I think it [the workload] has to affect, definitely, because it's the third game. It's the worst scenario – it's game, two days, game, two days, game. "In terms of the schedule, we haven't been lucky because it's true that after this one we have a little bit more [time] before we play Bournemouth. "Also we had a little bit more [time] between Ipswich and Atletico Madrid, and you notice if it's four or five days in comparison to two, three days. It's a massive difference but it is what it is. "I think after the international break also we have this period, I think, we are playing in nine, 10 days, four games or something like this. So, we have to get used to this." He continued: "You can decide and put the same players [in] every game. The problem is there is going to be a moment where they are going to be very tired and there is more risk of injury. But that's why we cannot say it doesn't work for anyone. "There are players who play every three days, they have no issues, they are very robust, they can accept it, their performances don't change too much. And there are other players where the risk is bigger, the performances are different. "And also we are in a process where I have to learn who is ready to play three or four games in a row every two or three days and who needs a rest so the performance level doesn't get affected. "I think I have it in my mind quite clear with some of them but with others it's new even for them because they haven't played as many games and we are learning." Asked about Liverpool's options between the posts, Iraola replied: "I think there are little doubts with Ali [Becker]. He's proven, he's playing very well. "I also rate Giorgi very highly. I know him from his years also in Spain. I told him we tried to sign him for Bournemouth before I came here. "For me, he's a very good 'keeper and he's going to start tomorrow, yes." Joe Gomez is fit again following the muscle injury he sustained in pre-season. "I think he's going to be available for tomorrow and now it's a matter of deciding how much he can play and what is the best thing to do," Iraola said. Conor Bradley, Federico Chiesa, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni remain sidelined. For Tottenham, Sandro Tonali is absent due to a knock, and Dejan Kulusevski and Pedro Porro are also out. Forward Richarlison will not feature, but Destiny Udogie is available after he missed the goalless draw with Everton last Saturday. Head coach Roberto De Zerbi told reporters on Monday: "Kulusevski is not available. Pedro is still not available. Udogie, yes. "Richarlison, nothing has changed for the Carabao Cup or Premier League, the situation is the same. No [he won't be involved]." On his selection plans for the tie, De Zerbi said: "The team selection is not difficult because I am lucky to have these players. I am convinced of the qualities of the players. "I think Lucas Bergvall is not other players. Mathys Tel also. And then we have to analyse the other players, maybe the players that didn't play enough. "I am lucky because in central defence I have Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky van de Ven, top centre-backs, but also Ben Davies, Marcos Senesi, Tosin [Adarabioyo] are not less than Van Hecke and Van de Ven." De Zerbi said 'I don't know' regarding a potential senior debut for academy player Luca Williams-Barnett and added: "I would like to play with the same attitude as in the Premier League. The attitude and spirit the same. "Many players need to play. Maybe not 90 minutes but 30 minutes. It is a real game. It is important." Legendary former Liverpool left-back Andy Robertson could make his first appearance against the Reds since he signed for Tottenham in the summer. title: Blizzard just announced Diablo V, and this time Diablo actually won - TechSpot
content:
Hellish Surprise: During the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony, Blizzard made an announcement no one could have foreseen. The studio is working on a new Diablo game, and players will get their hands on the new action-RPG experience sooner than expected. Diablo V is still years away from store shelves, but Blizzard is speeding up the franchise's development in a rather significant way. Three years after releasing Diablo IV, Blizzard is already hard at work on a new entry in the popular ARPG franchise. Diablo V will be built exclusively around the titular villain, who was conspicuously absent from the previous game, while players will reportedly face a much darker world where the "Prime Evil" has already won. Blizzard's announcement during BlizzCon 2026 was surprisingly rich with early details about the game's new features and changes. Diablo V is set 100 years after the story told in Diablo IV, and seven years after the Lord of Terror turned Sanctuary into his own hellish, post-apocalyptic dominion. Blizzard showed a brief teaser trailer depicting some telling signs that these are, indeed, the end times. Most humans are now worshiping Diablo, while angels are being crucified by the thousands. Even compared to Diablo's classic dark fantasy themes, Diablo V is shaping up to bring an even darker turn to the lore Blizzard North conceived three decades ago. The game is set in Westmarch, one of Sanctuary's Western kingdoms. There are no more "heroes" to save the day, although players will take on the role of the Heir to Westmarch's royal lineage. Just as it did with Mephisto in Diablo IV, Blizzard is apparently giving the player's character a "unique" connection to the Lord of Terror himself. No towns or other safe places are left, which means players will have to wander through the game's hellish world with a caravan of survivors. The world is so desolate and brutal that quest-giving NPCs disappear altogether. Additional Diablo V details unveiled by Blizzard during BlizzCon 2026 include the three playable classes available from the start: the "agile" Demon Hunter, the melee-focused Monk, and the brand-new class of disease-spreading Plague Knight. Monk was definitely one of the most enjoyable ways to play Diablo III, so I'm looking forward to trying a modern rendition of the class already. Diablo V will double down on "darkness" after the rose-tinted world of Diablo III, and will bring back some classic, most-requested features of the franchise such as gear-based "green" sets. The game is set to arrive in spring 2029, which gives Blizzard years to work through the massive feedback players will certainly provide. Some Diablo enthusiasts have indeed already expressed their dissatisfaction with Blizzard's premature announcement. Diablo V could be released with the shortest gap in the series, coming just six years after Diablo IV. Players had to wait 12 years between Diablo II and Diablo III, while Diablo IV came out 11 years after the previous chapter. I finished recording and editing hours of Diablo III gameplay for my YT channel just recently, and I still have to purchase Diablo IV to start digging into the new world. Blizzard explained that Diablo V was announced years in advance because the company is confident in the saga's appeal. The game is still going to "ship big" and on time, the company said. Players will be able to finish the experience solo or together with friends in multiplayer, although Blizzard is still refusing to define Diablo as an MMO title despite players' actual experience with Diablo IV. As an old-time Diablo II enthusiast, I consider the expression "Diablo MMO" to be the worst gaming insult I could ever receive. About
